title: JEE Main 2026 · 24 Jan · Shift 1 (recreated)

qs.stem: Let α, β ∈ R be such that the function f(x) = 2α(x<sup>2</sup> − 2) + 2βx for x < 1, and (α + 3)x + (α − β) for x ≥ 1, is differentiable at all x ∈ R. Then 34(α + β) is equal to :
steps: Continuity at x = 1: −2α + 2β = (α + 3) + (α − β), so 3β = 4α + 3.
Derivatives at x = 1 must match: left 4α + 2β, right α + 3, so 3α + 2β = 3.
Substituting β = (4α + 3)/3 gives 17α = 3, so α = 3/17 and β = 21/17.

qs.stem: The mean and variance of a data of 10 observations are 10 and 2, respectively. If an observations α in this data is replaced by β, then the mean and variance become 10.1 and 1.99, respectively. Then α + β equals :
steps: Sum of data: 100 originally, 101 after replacement, so β − α = 1.
Sum of squares: 10(2 + 100) = 1020 originally; 10(1.99 + 102.01) = 1040 after, so β<sup>2</sup> − α<sup>2</sup> = 20.
(β + α)(β − α) = 20 with β − α = 1 gives α + β = 20.

qs.stem: Let S = 1/25! + 1/(3! 23!) + 1/(5! 21!) + … up to 13 terms. If 13S = 2<sup>k</sup>/n!, k ∈ N, then n + k is equal to :
steps: The terms are 1/(r!(26 − r)!) for odd r = 1, 3, …, 25 (13 terms), so S = (1/26!)[<sup>26</sup>C<sub>1</sub> + <sup>26</sup>C<sub>3</sub> + … + <sup>26</sup>C<sub>25</sub>].
The sum of odd-place binomial coefficients is 2<sup>25</sup>, so S = 2<sup>25</sup>/26!.

qs.stem: If the domain of the function f(x) = log<sub>(10x<sup>2</sup> − 17x + 7)</sub>(18x<sup>2</sup> − 11x + 1) is (−∞, a) ∪ (b, c) ∪ (d, ∞) − {e}, then 90(a + b + c + d + e) equals :
steps: Argument positive: (2x − 1)(9x − 1) > 0, so x < 1/9 or x > 1/2.
Base positive and not 1: (x − 1)(10x − 7) > 0 gives x < 7/10 or x > 1; base = 1 means (5x − 6)(2x − 1) = 0, so x = 6/5 or 1/2 are removed.
Intersection: (−∞, 1/9) ∪ (1/2, 7/10) ∪ (1, ∞) − {6/5}, so a = 1/9, b = 1/2, c = 7/10, d = 1, e = 6/5.

qs.stem: Consider an A.P. a<sub>1</sub>, a<sub>2</sub>, …, a<sub>n</sub>; a<sub>1</sub> > 0. If a<sub>2</sub> − a<sub>1</sub> = −3/4, a<sub>n</sub> = (1/4)a<sub>1</sub>, and ∑<sub>i=1</sub><sup>n</sup> a<sub>i</sub> = 525/2, then ∑<sub>i=1</sub><sup>17</sup> a<sub>i</sub> is equal to :
steps: d = −3/4. a<sub>n</sub> = a<sub>1</sub>/4 gives (n − 1)(3/4) = 3a<sub>1</sub>/4, so a<sub>1</sub> = n − 1.

Sum of n terms = (n/2)(a<sub>1</sub> + a<sub>n</sub>) = (n/2)(5a<sub>1</sub>/4) = 525/2, so n a<sub>1</sub> = 420, i.e. a<sub>1</sub>(a<sub>1</sub> + 1) = 420 and a<sub>1</sub> = 20 (positive), n = 21.

qs.stem: Let a circle of radius 4 pass through the origin O, the points A(−√3 a, 0) and B(0, −√2 b), where a and b are real parameters and ab ≠ 0. Then the locus of the centroid of ΔOAB is a circle of radius :
steps: Angle AOB is a right angle, so AB is a diameter of the circle: AB = 8, giving 3a<sup>2</sup> + 2b<sup>2</sup> = 64.
Centroid (h, k) = (−√3 a/3, −√2 b/3), so 3a<sup>2</sup> = 9h<sup>2</sup> and 2b<sup>2</sup> = 9k<sup>2</sup>.
9(h<sup>2</sup> + k<sup>2</sup>) = 64, so the locus is x<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup> = 64/9 with radius 8/3.

qs.stem: If the function f(x) = [e<sup>x</sup>(e<sup>tan x − x</sup> − 1) + log<sub>e</sub>(sec x + tan x) − x]/(tan x − x) is continuous at x = 0, then the value of f(0) is equal to :
steps: Split into two parts. First: e<sup>x</sup>(e<sup>tan x − x</sup> − 1)/(tan x − x) → 1 × 1 = 1 as x → 0.
Second: ln(sec x + tan x) = x + x<sup>3</sup>/6 + … and tan x − x = x<sup>3</sup>/3 + …, so [ln(sec x + tan x) − x]/(tan x − x) → (1/6)/(1/3) = 1/2.

qs.stem: Let A<sub>1</sub> be the bounded area enclosed by the curves y = x<sup>2</sup> + 2, x + y = 8 and y-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Let A<sub>2</sub> be the bounded area enclosed by the curves y = x<sup>2</sup> + 2, y<sup>2</sup> = x, x = 2, and y-axis that lies in the first quadrant. Then A<sub>1</sub> − A<sub>2</sub> is equal to :
steps: The parabola and line meet where x<sup>2</sup> + x − 6 = 0, i.e. x = 2. A<sub>1</sub> = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> (6 − x − x<sup>2</sup>) dx = 12 − 2 − 8/3 = 22/3.
A<sub>2</sub> = ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup> (x<sup>2</sup> + 2 − √x) dx = 8/3 + 4 − (2/3)(2√2) = 20/3 − 4√2/3.
A<sub>1</sub> − A<sub>2</sub> = 2/3 + 4√2/3 = (2/3)(2√2 + 1).

qs.stem: The value of (√3 cosec 20° − sec 20°)/(cos 20° cos 40° cos 60° cos 80°) is equal to :
steps: Numerator: (√3 cos 20° − sin 20°)/(sin 20° cos 20°) = 2 cos 50°/(sin 20° cos 20°) = 2 sin 40°/((1/2) sin 40°) = 4.
Denominator: cos 20° cos 40° cos 80° = 1/8, and cos 60° = 1/2, so the product is 1/16.
Value = 4 × 16 = 64.

qs.stem: From a lot containing 10 defective and 90 non-defective bulbs, 8 bulbs are selected one by one with replacement. Then the probability of getting at least 7 defective bulbs is :
steps: Each draw is defective with probability 1/10 (binomial, n = 8).
P(exactly 7) = <sup>8</sup>C<sub>7</sub>(1/10)<sup>7</sup>(9/10) = 72/10<sup>8</sup>.
P(exactly 8) = 1/10<sup>8</sup>, so P(at least 7) = 73/10<sup>8</sup>.

qs.stem: If cot x = 5/12 for some x ∈ (π, 3π/2), then sin 7x (cos 13x/2 + sin 13x/2) + cos 7x (cos 13x/2 − sin 13x/2) is equal to :
steps: Group terms: sin 7x cos(13x/2) − cos 7x sin(13x/2) = sin(x/2) and cos 7x cos(13x/2) + sin 7x sin(13x/2) = cos(x/2). So E = sin(x/2) + cos(x/2).
E<sup>2</sup> = 1 + sin x. In the third quadrant with cot x = 5/12, sin x = −12/13, so E<sup>2</sup> = 1/13.
x/2 lies in (π/2, 3π/4) where sin > |cos|, so E > 0 and E = 1/√13.

qs.stem: Let 729, 81, 9, 1, … be a sequence and P<sub>n</sub> denote the product of the first n terms of this sequence. If 2∑<sub>n=1</sub><sup>40</sup> (P<sub>n</sub>)<sup>1/n</sup> = (3<sup>α</sup> − 1)/3<sup>β</sup> and gcd(α, β) = 1, then α + β is equal to :
steps: The sequence is a GP with first term 3<sup>6</sup> and ratio 1/9, so a<sub>k</sub> = 3<sup>6 − 2(k−1)</sup> = 3<sup>8 − 2k</sup>.
P<sub>n</sub> = 3<sup>∑(8 − 2k)</sup> = 3<sup>8n − n(n+1)</sup> = 3<sup>n(7 − n)</sup>, so (P<sub>n</sub>)<sup>1/n</sup> = 3<sup>7 − n</sup>.
2∑<sub>n=1</sub><sup>40</sup> 3<sup>7−n</sup> = 2 · 3<sup>−33</sup>(3<sup>40</sup> − 1)/2 = (3<sup>40</sup> − 1)/3<sup>33</sup>.
α = 40, β = 33 (coprime), so α + β = 73.

qs.stem: Let S = {z ∈ C : |z − 6i|/|z − 2i| = 1 and |z − 8 + 2i|/|z + 2i| = 3/5}. Then ∑<sub>z∈S</sub> |z|<sup>2</sup> is equal to :
steps: |z − 6i| = |z − 2i| means z is equidistant from 6i and 2i, so Im z = 4. Write z = x + 4i.
5|z − 8 + 2i| = 3|z + 2i| gives 25[(x − 8)<sup>2</sup> + 36] = 9(x<sup>2</sup> + 36), i.e. x<sup>2</sup> − 25x + 136 = 0 with roots 8 and 17.

qs.stem: Let R be a relation defined on the set {1, 2, 3, 4} × {1, 2, 3, 4} by R = {((a, b), (c, d)) : 2a + 3b = 3c + 4d}. Then the number of elements in R is :
steps: Rewrite as 2(a − 2d) = 3(c − b): a − 2d must be a multiple of 3 (say 3k) and then c − b = 2k.
Pairs (a, d) with a − 2d a multiple of 3: (2,1) k=0; (4,2) k=0; (1,2) k=−1; (3,3) k=−1; (2,4) k=−2.
Pairs (b, c) with c − b = 2k: k = 0 gives 4, k = −1 gives 2, k = −2 gives 0.

qs.stem: Let the lines L1 : r = i + 2j + 3k + λ(2i + 3j + 4k), λ ∈ R and L2 : r = (4i + j) + μ(5i + 2j + k), μ ∈ R, intersect at the point R. Let P and Q be the points lying on lines L1 and L2, respectively, such that |PR| = √29 and |PQ| = √(47/3). If the point P lies in the first octant, then 27(QR)2 is equal to :
steps: Equate coordinates: 1 + 2λ = 4 + 5μ, 2 + 3λ = 1 + 2μ, 3 + 4λ = μ. These give λ = μ = −1, so R = (−1, −1, −1).
PR<sup>2</sup> = 29(λ + 1)<sup>2</sup> = 29 gives λ = 0 or −2; first octant needs P = (1, 2, 3).

qs.stem: Let each of the two ellipses E<sub>1</sub> : x<sup>2</sup>/a<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/b<sup>2</sup> = 1, (a > b) and E<sub>2</sub> : x<sup>2</sup>/A<sup>2</sup> + y<sup>2</sup>/B<sup>2</sup> = 1, (A < B) have eccentricity 4/5. Let the lengths of the latus recta of E<sub>1</sub> and E<sub>2</sub> be l<sub>1</sub> and l<sub>2</sub>, respectively, such that 2l<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = 9l<sub>2</sub>. If the distance between the foci of E<sub>1</sub> is 8, then the distance between the foci of E<sub>2</sub> is :
steps: For E<sub>1</sub>: 2ae = 8 with e = 4/5 gives a = 5, and b<sup>2</sup> = a<sup>2</sup>(1 − 16/25) = 9, so b = 3. l<sub>1</sub> = 2b<sup>2</sup>/a = 18/5.
2l<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup> = 9l<sub>2</sub> gives l<sub>2</sub> = 2(324/25)/9 = 72/25.
E<sub>2</sub> has major axis along y: A<sup>2</sup> = 9B<sup>2</sup>/25 and l<sub>2</sub> = 2A<sup>2</sup>/B = 18B/25 = 72/25, so B = 4.
Distance between foci = 2Be = 2 × 4 × 4/5 = 32/5.

qs.stem: The number of the real solutions of the equation : x|x + 3| + |x − 1| − 2 = 0 is :
steps: x ≥ 1: x<sup>2</sup> + 4x − 3 = 0, x = −2 ± √7; neither root is ≥ 1 (−2 + √7 ≈ 0.65), so no solution.
−3 ≤ x < 1: x<sup>2</sup> + 2x − 1 = 0, x = −1 ± √2; both (0.41 and −2.41) lie in the interval: 2 solutions.
x < −3: x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 1 = 0, x = −2 ± √3; only −2 − √3 ≈ −3.73 qualifies: 1 solution.
Total 3 real solutions.

qs.stem: Let A(1, 0), B(2, −1) and C(7/3, 4/3) be three points. If the equation of the bisector of the angle ABC is αx + βy = 5, then the value of α<sup>2</sup> + β<sup>2</sup> is :
steps: Line BA: x + y − 1 = 0. Line BC: slope 7, so 7x − y − 15 = 0.
Bisectors: 5(x + y − 1) = ±(7x − y − 15), giving −x + 3y + 5 = 0 or 3x + y − 5 = 0.
The internal bisector keeps A and C on opposite sides: 3x + y − 5 has values −2 at A and 10/3 at C, so it is the one. It passes through B and is 3x + y = 5, so α = 3, β = 1.
α<sup>2</sup> + β<sup>2</sup> = 10.

qs.stem: Let a = 2i + j − 2k, b = i + j and c = a × b. Let d be a vector such that |d − a| = √11, |c × d| = 3 and the angle between c and d is π/4. Then a · d is equal to :
steps: |c||d| sin(π/4) = 3 gives |d| = √2.
|d − a|2 = |d|2 + |a|2 − 2a·d = 2 + 9 − 2a·d = 11, so a·d = 0.

qs.stem: Let f(t) = ∫ [(1 − sin(log<sub>e</sub> t))/(1 − cos(log<sub>e</sub> t))] dt, t > 1. If f(e<sup>π/2</sup>) = −e<sup>π/2</sup> and f(e<sup>π/4</sup>) = αe<sup>π/4</sup>, then α equals :
steps: With θ = ln t: (1 − sin θ)/(1 − cos θ) = (1/2)cosec<sup>2</sup>(θ/2) − cot(θ/2).
Check that d/dt[−t cot(θ/2)] = −cot(θ/2) + (1/2)cosec<sup>2</sup>(θ/2), so f(t) = −t cot((ln t)/2) + C.
f(e<sup>π/2</sup>) = −e<sup>π/2</sup> cot(π/4) + C = −e<sup>π/2</sup> gives C = 0.
f(e<sup>π/4</sup>) = −e<sup>π/4</sup> cot(π/8) = −(√2 + 1)e<sup>π/4</sup>, so α = −1 − √2.

qs.stem: The number of 3 × 2 matrices A, which can be formed using the elements of the set {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} such that the sum of all the diagonal elements of A<sup>T</sup>A is 5, is ________.
steps: The trace of A<sup>T</sup>A equals the sum of squares of all six entries of A, so we need six entries from {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} with squares summing to 5.
Case 1: five entries ±1 and one 0: 6 positions for 0 and 2<sup>5</sup> sign choices = 192.
Case 2: one entry ±2, one entry ±1, four zeros (4 + 1 = 5): 6 × 5 position choices and 2 × 2 signs = 120.

qs.stem: Let a line L passing through the point P(1, 1, 1) be perpendicular to the lines (x − 4)/4 = (y − 1)/1 = (z − 1)/1 and (x − 17)/1 = (y − 71)/1 = z/0. Let the line L intersect the yz-plane at the point Q. Another line parallel to L and passing through the point S(1, 0, −1) intersects the yz-plane at the point R. Then the square of the area of the parallelogram PQRS is equal to ________.
steps: Direction of L = (4, 1, 1) × (1, 1, 0) = (−1, 1, 3).
L: (1 − λ, 1 + λ, 1 + 3λ); x = 0 gives λ = 1, Q = (0, 2, 4). Line through S: (1 − δ, δ, −1 + 3δ); x = 0 gives R = (0, 1, 2).
PQ = (−1, 1, 3), PS = (0, −1, −2); PQ × PS = (1, −2, 1).
Area<sup>2</sup> = 1 + 4 + 1 = 6.

qs.stem: Let (2α, α) be the largest interval in which the function f(t) = |t + 1|/t<sup>2</sup>, t < 0, is strictly decreasing. Then the local maximum value of the function g(x) = 2 log<sub>e</sub>(x − 2) + αx<sup>2</sup> + 4x − α, x > 2, is ________.
steps: For t < −1, f = −(t + 1)/t<sup>2</sup> and f′ = (t + 2)/t<sup>3</sup>, which is negative for −2 < t < −1. For −1 < t < 0, f′ > 0 (increasing); for t < −2, f′ > 0.
So f decreases exactly on (−2, −1): 2α = −2, α = −1.
g(x) = 2 ln(x − 2) − x<sup>2</sup> + 4x + 1 and g′(x) = 2/(x − 2) − 2x + 4 = 2(3 − x)(x − 1)/(x − 2), positive before 3 and negative after, so the maximum is at x = 3.

qs.stem: The number of numbers greater than 5000, less than 9000 and divisible by 3, that can be formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 5, 9, if the repetition of the digits is allowed, is ________.
steps: Four-digit numbers below 9000 and above 5000 must start with 5 (residue 2 mod 3). The last three digits must then have digit-sum ≡ 1 (mod 3).
Residue classes: 0 → {0, 9}, 1 → {1}, 2 → {2, 5}.
Residue patterns summing to 1: {0,0,1}: 3 × (2·2·1) = 12; {0,2,2}: 3 × (2·2·2) = 24; {1,1,2}: 3 × (1·1·2) = 6.

qs.stem: Let a differentiable function f satisfy the equation ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>36</sup> f(tx/36) dt = 4αf(x). If y = f(x) is a standard parabola passing through the points (2, 1) and (−4, β), then β<sup>α</sup> is equal to ________.
steps: Put z = tx/36: (36/x)∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> f(z) dz = 4αf(x), i.e. 9∫<sub>0</sub><sup>x</sup> f = αx f(x).
Differentiate: 9f = αf + αx f′, so f′/f = (9 − α)/(αx) and f = C x<sup>(9−α)/α</sup>.
A parabola y = Cx<sup>2</sup> needs (9 − α)/α = 2, so α = 3 (the exponent 1/2 would give y<sup>2</sup> = x/2, which cannot pass through x = −4). Through (2, 1): C = 1/4.
f(−4) = 16/4 = 4 = β, so β<sup>α</sup> = 4<sup>3</sup> = 64.

qs.stem: An unpolarised light is incident at an interface of two dielectric media having refractive indices of 2 (incident medium) and 2√3 (medium) respectively. To satisfy the condition that reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other, the angle of incidence is ________.
steps: Reflected and refracted rays being perpendicular means the incidence angle is Brewster's angle.
tan θ<sub>B</sub> = n<sub>2</sub>/n<sub>1</sub> = 2√3/2 = √3.
So θ<sub>B</sub> = 60°.

qs.stem:
Density of water at 4 °C and 20 °C are 1000 kg/m3 and 998 kg/m3 respectively. The increase in internal energy of 4 kg of water when it is heated from 4 °C to 20 °C is _______ J.
(specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J/kg. and 1 atmospheric pressure = 105 Pa)
steps: Heat supplied Q = m s ΔT = 4 × 4200 × 16 = 268800 J (taking s as 4200 J/kg·K, the printed unit being garbled).
Volume rises by ΔV = 4/998 − 4/1000 ≈ 8.02 × 10<sup>−6</sup> m<sup>3</sup>, so work done by water W = PΔV ≈ 0.80 J.
ΔU = Q − W = 268800 − 0.8 = 268799.2 J.

qs.stem:
The electrostatic potential in a charged spherical region of radius r varies as V = ar3 + b, where a and b are constants. The total charge in the sphere of unit radius is α × πaε0. The value of α is ________.
(permittivity of vacuum is ε0)
steps: Radial field E = −dV/dr = −3ar<sup>2</sup>.
Gauss's law: q = ε<sub>0</sub>E(4πr<sup>2</sup>) = −12πaε<sub>0</sub>r<sup>4</sup>.
At r = 1: q = −12 πaε<sub>0</sub>, so α = −12.

qs.stem: The exit surface of a prism with refractive index n is coated with a material having refractive index n/2. When this prism is set for minimum angle of deviation, it exactly meets the condition of critical angle. The prism angle is ________.
steps: At minimum deviation the ray inside is symmetric, so the angle of incidence on the exit face is r = A/2.
Critical angle at the n to n/2 boundary: n sin(A/2) = (n/2) sin 90°.
sin(A/2) = 1/2, so A/2 = 30° and A = 60°.

qs.stem: For the series LCR circuit connected with 220 V, 50 Hz a.c source as shown in the figure, the power factor is a/10. The value of a is _________.
steps: Net reactance X = |X<sub>L</sub> − X<sub>C</sub>| = |70 − 150| = 80 Ω.
Impedance Z = √(60<sup>2</sup> + 80<sup>2</sup>) = 100 Ω.
Power factor = R/Z = 60/100 = 6/10, so a = 6.

qs.stem: Two electrons are moving in orbits of two hydrogen like atoms with speeds 3 × 10<sup>5</sup> m/s and 2.5 × 10<sup>5</sup> m/s respectively. If the radii of these orbits are nearly same then the possible order of energy states are ________ respectively.
steps: Bohr model: v ∝ Z/n and r ∝ n<sup>2</sup>/Z.
Equal radii give n<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>/Z<sub>1</sub> = n<sub>2</sub><sup>2</sup>/Z<sub>2</sub>, so Z<sub>1</sub>/Z<sub>2</sub> = (n<sub>1</sub>/n<sub>2</sub>)<sup>2</sup>.
The speed ratio gives (Z<sub>1</sub>/Z<sub>2</sub>)(n<sub>2</sub>/n<sub>1</sub>) = 3/2.5 = 6/5, so n<sub>1</sub>/n<sub>2</sub> = 6/5.
Only 6 and 5 fits this ratio.

qs.stem:
Three masses 200 kg, 300 kg and 400 kg are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with sides 20 m . They are rearranged on the vertices of a bigger triangle of side 25 m and with the same centre. The work done in this process _______J.
(Gravitational constant G = 6.7 × 10−11 N m2/kg2)
steps: For an equilateral triangle of side s, U = −G(m<sub>1</sub>m<sub>2</sub> + m<sub>2</sub>m<sub>3</sub> + m<sub>3</sub>m<sub>1</sub>)/s.
Sum of products = 60000 + 120000 + 80000 = 2.6 × 10<sup>5</sup> kg<sup>2</sup>.
W = ΔU = G(2.6 × 10<sup>5</sup>)(1/20 − 1/25) = 6.7 × 10<sup>−11</sup> × 2.6 × 10<sup>5</sup> × 0.01 ≈ 1.74 × 10<sup>−7</sup> J.

qs.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon.
Statement II : For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: The binding energy per nucleon curve rises up to about Fe (around 8.8 MeV) and then falls for heavier nuclei, so Statement I is false.
Nuclei change (fusion of light, fission of heavy) towards higher binding energy per nucleon, i.e. greater stability, so Statement II is true.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

qs.stem: Two resistors of 100 Ω each are connected in series with a 9 V battery. A voltmeter of 400 Ω resistance is connected to measure the voltage drop across one of the resistors. The voltmeter reading is ______V.
steps: Voltmeter in parallel with a 100 Ω resistor: (100 × 400)/(500) = 80 Ω.
Total resistance = 100 + 80 = 180 Ω, so I = 9/180 = 0.05 A.
Reading = 0.05 × 80 = 4 V.

qs.stem: There are three co-centric conducting spherical shells A, B and C of radii a, b and c respectively (c > b > a) and they are charged with charge q<sub>1</sub>, q<sub>2</sub> and q<sub>3</sub> respectively. The potentials of the spheres A, B and C respectively, are :
steps: Potential of a shell = its own charge over its radius plus contributions of other shells (inside a shell, potential from it is kq/R; outside, kq/r).
V<sub>A</sub> = k(q<sub>1</sub>/a + q<sub>2</sub>/b + q<sub>3</sub>/c).
V<sub>B</sub> = k((q<sub>1</sub>+q<sub>2</sub>)/b + q<sub>3</sub>/c), and V<sub>C</sub> = k(q<sub>1</sub>+q<sub>2</sub>+q<sub>3</sub>)/c, which is option 2.

qs.stem: A brass wire of length 2 m and radius 1 mm at 27 °C is held taut between two rigid supports. Initially it was cooled to a temperature of −43 °C creating a tension T in the wire. The temperature to which the wire has to be cooled in order to increase the tension in it to 1.4 T, is ________°C.
steps: Rigid supports fix the length; thermal contraction is resisted, so T = YAαΔθ with Δθ measured from 27 °C.
First case: Δθ = 27 − (−43) = 70 K.
For 1.4 T: Δθ = 1.4 × 70 = 98 K, so final temperature = 27 − 98 = −71 °C.

qs.stem: A spring of force constant 15 N/m is cut into two pieces. If the ratio of their length is 1 : 3, then the force constant of smaller piece is ________ N/m.
steps: Spring constant is inversely proportional to length, so kl is constant.
Smaller piece has length l/4 (ratio 1:3 of total l).
k' = k × l/(l/4) = 4 × 15 = 60 N/m.

qs.stem: Two resistors 2 Ω and 3 Ω are connected in the gaps of bridge as shown in figure. The null point is obtained with the contact of jockey at some point on wire XY. When an unknown resistor is connected in parallel with 3 Ω resistor, the null point is shifted by 22.5 cm toward Y. The resistance of unknown resistor is _________Ω.
steps: Initial balance on a 100 cm wire: 2/l = 3/(100 − l), so l = 40 cm.
New null point at 40 + 22.5 = 62.5 cm, leaving 37.5 cm; the right gap becomes 3R/(3+R).

qs.stem: A cylindrical block of mass M and area of cross section A is floating in a liquid of density ρ and with its axis vertical. When depressed a little and released the block starts oscillating. The period of oscillation is ________.
steps: Pushing the block down by x adds a buoyant force ρAgx opposing the displacement.
M(d<sup>2</sup>x/dt<sup>2</sup>) = −ρAgx, so ω<sup>2</sup> = ρAg/M.
T = 2π/ω = 2π√(M/(ρAg)).

qs.stem:
Match the List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Magnetic induction; B. Magnetic flux; C. Magnetic permeability; D. Self inductance.
List-II: I. M L T−2 A−2; II. M L2 T−2 A−2; III. M L0 T−2 A−1; IV. M L2 T−2 A−1.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: B = F/(IL) = M T<sup>−2</sup> A<sup>−1</sup> (III).
Flux = B × area = M L<sup>2</sup> T<sup>−2</sup> A<sup>−1</sup> (IV).
μ<sub>0</sub> = F/I<sup>2</sup> = M L T<sup>−2</sup> A<sup>−2</sup> (I); L = flux/I = M L<sup>2</sup> T<sup>−2</sup> A<sup>−2</sup> (II).

qs.stem:
Two masses 400 g and 350 g are suspended from the ends of a light string passing over a heavy pulley of radius 2 cm. When released from rest the heavier mass is observed to fall 81 cm in 9 s. The rotational inertia of the pulley is ________ kg.m2.
(g = 9.8 m/s2)
steps: a = (m<sub>1</sub> − m<sub>2</sub>)g/(m<sub>1</sub> + m<sub>2</sub> + I/r<sup>2</sup>), so 0.02 = 0.05 × 9.8/(0.75 + I/r<sup>2</sup>), giving I/r<sup>2</sup> = 23.75 kg.
I = 23.75 × (0.02)<sup>2</sup> = 9.5 × 10<sup>−3</sup> kg m<sup>2</sup>.

qs.stem: In a microscope of tube length 10 cm two convex lenses are arranged with focal length of 2 cm and 5 cm. Total magnification obtained with this system for normal adjustment is (5)<sup>k</sup>. The value of k is ________.
steps: Compound microscope with final image at infinity (normal adjustment) uses M = (L/f<sub>o</sub>)(D/f<sub>e</sub>) with D = 25 cm.
Objective is the 2 cm lens, eyepiece the 5 cm lens: M = (10/2)(25/5) = 5 × 5 = 25.

qs.stem: Three charges + 2q, +3q and –4q are situated at (0, –3a), (2a, 0) and (–2a, 0) respectively in the x y plane. The resultant dipole moment about origin is ________.
steps: Dipole moment of a charge system about the origin: p = ∑qr.
+2q at (0, −3a): −6qa j; +3q at (2a, 0): +6qa i; −4q at (−2a, 0): +8qa i.
p = 14qa i − 6qa j = 2qa(7i − 3j).

qs.stem:
A boy throws a ball into air at 45° from the horizontal to land it on a roof of a building of height H. If the ball attains maximum height in 2 s and lands on the building in 3 s after launch, then value of H is ______ m.
(g = 10 m/s2)
steps: Time to top is u sin 45°/g = 2 s, so the vertical component is 20 m/s (u = 20√2 m/s).
Height at t = 3 s: H = 20(3) − (1/2)(10)(3)<sup>2</sup> = 60 − 45 = 15 m.

qs.stem:
Match the List-I with List-II.
List-I: A. Radio-wave; B. Micro-wave; C. Infrared-wave; D. X-ray.
List-II: I. is produced by Magnetron valve; II. due to change in the vibrational modes of atoms; III. due to inner shell electrons moving from higher energy level to lower energy level; IV. due to rapid acceleration of electrons.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
steps: Radio waves arise from accelerated electrons in conductors (IV).
Microwaves are generated in a magnetron valve (I).
Infrared comes from changes in vibrational modes of atoms/molecules (II); X-rays from inner-shell electron transitions (III).
So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

qs.stem: A gas of certain mass filled in a closed cylinder at a pressure of 3.23 kPa has temperature 50 °C. The gas is now heated to double its temperature. The modified pressure is _______ Pa.
steps: Closed cylinder: volume constant, so P/T is constant (T in kelvin).
Initial T = 323 K; "double" is read on the Celsius scale, giving 100 °C = 373 K.

qs.stem: In the given figure the blocks A, B and C weigh 4 kg, 6 kg and 8 kg respectively. The co-efficient of sliding friction between any two surfaces is 0.5. The force F required to slide the block C with constant speed is ________N. (Use g = 10 m/s2)
steps: Block A sits on B, B on C, C on the ground; a string over a pulley fixed at the wall joins B and C, so B moves opposite to C. Friction between each pair of sliding surfaces is μN.
Friction: ground on C, f<sub>1</sub> = 0.5 × 18 × 10 = 90 N; B on C, f<sub>2</sub> = 0.5 × 10 × 10 = 50 N; A on B, f<sub>3</sub> = 0.5 × 4 × 10 = 20 N.
Equilibrium of B: T = f<sub>2</sub> + f<sub>3</sub> = 70 N.
Equilibrium of C: F = f<sub>1</sub> + f<sub>2</sub> + T = 90 + 50 + 70 = 210 N.

qs.stem: Sixty four rain drops of radius 1 mm each falling down with a terminal velocity of 10 cm/s coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of bigger drop is ________ cm/s.
steps: Volume conservation: 64 × (4/3)πr<sup>3</sup> = (4/3)πR<sup>3</sup>, so R = 4r.
Terminal velocity v<sub>T</sub> ∝ r<sup>2</sup>, so the new velocity is 16 times the old.
v<sub>T</sub>' = 16 × 10 = 160 cm/s.

qs.stem: A voltage regulating circuit consisting of Zener diode, having break-down voltage of 10 V and maximum power dissipation of 0.4 W, is operated at 15 V. The approximate value of protective resistance in this circuit is _______Ω.
steps: Maximum Zener current I = P/V<sub>z</sub> = 0.4/10 = 0.04 A.
Voltage across the series resistor = 15 − 10 = 5 V.

qs.stem: A short bar magnet placed with its axis at 30° with an external field of 800 Gauss, experiences a torque of 0.016 N.m. The work done in moving it from most stable to most unstable position is a × 10<sup>−3</sup> J. The value of a is ________.
steps: B = 800 G = 0.08 T. Torque τ = MB sin 30° gives M = 0.016/(0.08 × 0.5) = 0.4 A m<sup>2</sup>.
Work from θ = 0 to 180° = MB(1 − cos 180°) = 2MB.
W = 2 × 0.4 × 0.08 = 0.064 J = 64 × 10<sup>−3</sup> J, so a = 64.

qs.stem: Consider the following two reactions A and B: (A) phenol + Na → main product + gas (x); (B) benzoic acid + NaHCO<sub>3</sub> → main product + gas (y). Numerical value of [molar mass of x + molar mass of y] is ______.
steps: Phenol is acidic enough to react with sodium metal: 2C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 2Na → 2C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>ONa + H<sub>2</sub>, so gas x = H<sub>2</sub> (2 g/mol).

Benzoic acid is a stronger acid than carbonic acid and liberates CO<sub>2</sub> from bicarbonate: C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>COOH + NaHCO<sub>3</sub> → C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>COONa + H<sub>2</sub>O + CO<sub>2</sub>, so gas y = CO<sub>2</sub> (44 g/mol).

qs.stem: Arrange the following carbanions in the decreasing order of stability. I. p-Br-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>; II. C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>; III. p-CH<sub>3</sub>O-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>; IV. p-CHO-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>; V. p-CH<sub>3</sub>-C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>-CH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup>. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A carbanion is stabilised by electron-withdrawing groups and destabilised by electron-donating groups on the ring.
p-CHO withdraws strongly by −M and −I, so IV is the most stable; p-Br withdraws by −I (outweighing weak +M), so I is next, above the unsubstituted II.
p-CH<sub>3</sub> donates by +I and hyperconjugation (V), while p-OCH<sub>3</sub> donates strongly by +M (III), so III is the least stable.
Order: IV > I > II > V > III.

qs.stem: Consider a mixture 'X' which is made by dissolving 0.4 mol of [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>]Br and 0.4 mol of [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>Br]SO<sub>4</sub> in water to make 4 L of solution. When 2 L of mixture 'X' is allowed to react with excess of AgNO<sub>3</sub>, it forms precipitate 'Y'. The rest 2 L of mixture 'X' reacts with excess BaCl<sub>2</sub> to form precipitate 'Z'. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
steps: Each 2 L portion holds half of the amounts: 0.2 mol of each complex.
With AgNO<sub>3</sub>, only ionisable Br<sup>−</sup> from [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>]Br precipitates: Y = AgBr, 0.2 mol (so options 3 and 4 fail).
With BaCl<sub>2</sub>, only ionisable SO<sub>4</sub><sup>2−</sup> from [Co(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>5</sub>Br]SO<sub>4</sub> precipitates: Z = BaSO<sub>4</sub>, 0.2 mol.

qs.stem: A solution is prepared by dissolving 0.3 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'A' of molar mass 60 g mol<sup>−1</sup> and 0.9 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'B' of molar mass 180 g mol<sup>−1</sup> in 100 mL H<sub>2</sub>O at 27°C. Osmotic pressure of the solution will be [Given: R = 0.082 L atm K<sup>−1</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup>]
steps: π = CRT = 0.10 × 0.082 × 300 = 2.46 atm.

qs.stem: 'W' g of a non-volatile electrolyte solid solute of molar mass 'M' g mol<sup>−1</sup> when dissolved in 100 mL water, decreases vapour pressure of water from 640 mm Hg to 600 mm Hg. If aqueous solution of the electrolyte boils at 375 K and K<sub>b</sub> for water is 0.52 K kg mol<sup>−1</sup>, then the mole fraction of the electrolyte solute (x<sub>2</sub>) in the solution can be expressed as (Given: density of water = 1 g/mL and boiling point of water = 373 K)
steps: Boiling point elevation: ΔT<sub>b</sub> = i K<sub>b</sub> m gives 2 = i × 0.52 × (W/M)/0.1, so i(W/M) = 0.2/0.52.
Relative lowering of vapour pressure: (640 − 600)/640 = 1/16 = i x<sub>2</sub>.

qs.stem: Among the following, the CORRECT combinations are: A. IF<sub>3</sub> → T-shaped (sp<sup>3</sup>d); B. IF<sub>5</sub> → Square pyramidal (sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>2</sup>); C. IF<sub>7</sub> → Pentagonal bipyramidal (sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>3</sup>); D. ClO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> → Square planar (sp<sup>2</sup>d). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: IF<sub>3</sub>: 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs, sp<sup>3</sup>d, T-shaped (A correct).
IF<sub>5</sub>: 5 bp + 1 lp, sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>2</sup>, square pyramidal (B correct); IF<sub>7</sub>: 7 bp, sp<sup>3</sup>d<sup>3</sup>, pentagonal bipyramidal (C correct).
ClO<sub>4</sub><sup>−</sup> has four bond pairs and no lone pair on Cl, so it is sp<sup>3</sup> tetrahedral, not square planar (D wrong). Answer: A, B and C only.

qs.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement I: 'C−Cl' bond is stronger in CH<sub>2</sub>=CH−Cl than CH<sub>3</sub>−CH<sub>2</sub>−Cl. Statement II: The given optically active molecule, a tertiary chloride with Ph, Me, Et and Cl on the stereocentre carbon (2-chloro-2-phenylbutane, one enantiomer), on hydrolysis gives a solution that can rotate the plane polarized light. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: In vinyl chloride the Cl lone pair is delocalised into the C=C (resonance) and the carbon is sp<sup>2</sup>, giving partial double-bond character, so the C−Cl bond is stronger than in chloroethane. Statement I is true.
The tertiary benzylic chloride ionises by S<sub>N</sub>1 through a planar carbocation, which is attacked from both faces to give a racemic alcohol.
A racemic mixture is optically inactive, so Statement II is false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: Given below are statements about some molecules/ions. Identify the CORRECT statements. A. The dipole moment value of NF<sub>3</sub> is higher than that of NH<sub>3</sub>. B. The dipole moment value of BeH<sub>2</sub> is zero. C. The bond order of O<sub>2</sub><sup>2−</sup> and F<sub>2</sub> is same. D. The formal charge on the central oxygen atom of ozone is −1. E. In NO<sub>2</sub>, all the three atoms satisfy the octet rule, hence it is very stable. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: A false: in NH<sub>3</sub> the N–H bond dipoles add to the lone-pair dipole (1.47 D) while in NF<sub>3</sub> the N–F dipoles oppose it (0.24 D).
B true: BeH<sub>2</sub> is linear and symmetric. C true: O<sub>2</sub><sup>2−</sup> (peroxide) and F<sub>2</sub> both have bond order 1.
D false: the central O of ozone carries +1. E false: NO<sub>2</sub> has an odd electron on N, so N has no octet. Answer: B and C only.

qs.stem: At 27°C in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by 10 kJ mol<sup>−1</sup>. The logarithm of ratio of (k (catalysed))/(k (uncatalysed)) is.... (Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
steps: With equal A, k<sub>cat</sub>/k<sub>uncat</sub> = e<sup>ΔE<sub>a</sub>/RT</sup>, so log(ratio) = ΔE<sub>a</sub>/(2.303 RT).

qs.stem: Given below are two statements: Statement I: K > Mg > Al > B is the correct order in terms of metallic character. Statement II: Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
steps: Metallic character falls with increasing electronegativity (K 0.8, Mg 1.2, Al 1.5, B 2.0), so K > Mg > Al > B is correct: Statement I true.
For anions the ionic radius exceeds the atomic radius (Cl<sup>−</sup> > Cl), so 'always' fails: Statement II false.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

qs.stem: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. List-I (Isothermal process for ideal gas system): A. Reversible expansion; B. Free expansion; C. Irreversible expansion; D. Irreversible compression. List-II (Work done, V<sub>f</sub> > V<sub>i</sub>): I. w = 0; II. w = −nRT ln(V<sub>f</sub>/V<sub>i</sub>); III. w = −p<sub>ex</sub>(V<sub>f</sub> − V<sub>i</sub>); IV. w = −p<sub>ex</sub>(V<sub>i</sub> − V<sub>f</sub>). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Reversible isothermal expansion: w = −nRT ln(V<sub>f</sub>/V<sub>i</sub>), so A-II.
Free expansion (p<sub>ex</sub> = 0): w = 0, so B-I.

Irreversible expansion against p<sub>ex</sub>: w = −p<sub>ex</sub>(V<sub>f</sub> − V<sub>i</sub>), so C-III; irreversible compression from V<sub>f</sub> to V<sub>i</sub> gives w = −p<sub>ex</sub>(V<sub>i</sub> − V<sub>f</sub>), so D-IV.

qs.stem: Consider three metal chlorides x, y and z, where x is water soluble at room temperature, y is sparingly soluble in water at room temperature and z is soluble in hot water. x, y and z are respectively
steps: CuCl<sub>2</sub> dissolves readily in water at room temperature (x).
AgCl is only sparingly soluble in cold water (y).
PbCl<sub>2</sub> is poorly soluble in cold water but dissolves in hot water (z). Only option 3 fits all three.

qs.stem: A hydroxy compound (X) with molar mass 122 g mol<sup>−1</sup> is acetylated with acetic anhydride, using a large excess of the reagent ensuring complete acetylation of all hydroxyl groups. The product obtained has a molar mass of 290 g mol<sup>−1</sup>. The number of hydroxyl groups present in compound (X) is:
steps: Each −OH becomes −OCOCH<sub>3</sub>: H (1) is replaced by COCH<sub>3</sub> (43), a mass gain of 42 per group.
Total gain = 290 − 122 = 168.
Number of OH groups = 168/42 = 4.

qs.stem: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. List-I Chloro derivative: A. Vinyl Chloride; B. Benzyl Chloride; C. Alkyl Chloride; D. Allyl Chloride. List-II Example: I. CH<sub>2</sub>=CH−CH<sub>2</sub>Cl; II. CH<sub>3</sub>−CH(Cl)CH<sub>3</sub>; III. CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCl; IV. C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>5</sub>−CH(Cl)−CH<sub>3</sub> (benzene ring bearing a CH(Cl)CH<sub>3</sub> group). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
steps: Vinyl chloride has Cl on a C=C carbon: CH<sub>2</sub>=CHCl (III).
Benzyl-type chloride has Cl on a carbon directly attached to the benzene ring (IV); an alkyl chloride is isopropyl chloride (II).
Allyl chloride has Cl on the sp<sup>3</sup> carbon next to C=C: CH<sub>2</sub>=CH−CH<sub>2</sub>Cl (I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

qs.stem: The correct stability order of the following diazonium salts is: (A) p-methoxybenzenediazonium chloride; (B) p-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride; (C) benzenediazonium chloride; (D) p-cyanobenzenediazonium chloride.
steps: The diazonium cation is stabilised by electron-donating groups (which push electron density toward the positive N) and destabilised by electron-withdrawing groups.
OCH<sub>3</sub> (+M) is donating, so A is the most stable, then unsubstituted C.
CN and NO<sub>2</sub> both withdraw, NO<sub>2</sub> more strongly, so D > B. Order: A > C > D > B.

qs.stem: The hydrogen spectrum consists of several spectral lines in Lyman series (L<sub>1</sub>, L<sub>2</sub>, L<sub>3</sub> ...; L<sub>1</sub> has lowest energy among Lyman series). Similarly it consists of several spectral lines in Balmer series (B<sub>1</sub>, B<sub>2</sub>, B<sub>3</sub> ...; B<sub>1</sub> has lowest energy among Balmer lines). The energy of L<sub>1</sub> is x times the energy of B<sub>1</sub>. The value of x is ____ × 10<sup>−1</sup>. (Nearest integer)
steps: L<sub>1</sub> is the 2 → 1 transition: E ∝ 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.
B<sub>1</sub> is the 3 → 2 transition: E ∝ 1/4 − 1/9 = 5/36.
x = (3/4)/(5/36) = 27/5 = 5.4 = 54 × 10<sup>−1</sup>, so the answer is 54.

qs.stem: In Dumas method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.50 g of an organic compound gave 70 mL of nitrogen collected at 300 K and 715 mm pressure. The percentage of nitrogen in the organic compound is ________ %. (Aqueous tension at 300 K is 15 mm).
steps: Dry nitrogen pressure = 715 − 15 = 700 mm Hg = 700/760 atm.
n(N<sub>2</sub>) = PV/RT = (700/760)(0.070)/(0.082 × 300) ≈ 2.62 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol.
Mass of N = 2 × 2.62 × 10<sup>−3</sup> × 14 ≈ 0.0734 g; % N = 0.0734/0.50 × 100 ≈ 14.7, i.e. 15 to the nearest integer.

qs.stem: Consider two Group IV metal ions X<sup>2+</sup> and Y<sup>2+</sup>. A solution containing 0.01 M X<sup>2+</sup> and 0.01 M Y<sup>2+</sup> is saturated with H<sub>2</sub>S. The pH at which the metal sulphide YS will form as a precipitate is ________. (Nearest integer) (Given: K<sub>sp</sub>(XS) = 1 × 10<sup>−22</sup> at 25°C, K<sub>sp</sub>(YS) = 4 × 10<sup>−16</sup> at 25°C, [H<sub>2</sub>S] = 0.1 M in solution, K<sub>a1</sub> × K<sub>a2</sub>(H<sub>2</sub>S) = 1.0 × 10<sup>−21</sup>, log 2 = 0.30, log 3 = 0.48, log 5 = 0.70)
steps: YS just precipitates when [Y<sup>2+</sup>][S<sup>2−</sup>] = K<sub>sp</sub>: [S<sup>2−</sup>] = 4 × 10<sup>−16</sup>/0.01 = 4 × 10<sup>−14</sup> M.
K<sub>a1</sub>K<sub>a2</sub> = [H<sup>+</sup>]<sup>2</sup>[S<sup>2−</sup>]/[H<sub>2</sub>S], so [H<sup>+</sup>]<sup>2</sup> = (10<sup>−21</sup> × 0.1)/(4 × 10<sup>−14</sup>) = 2.5 × 10<sup>−9</sup>.
[H<sup>+</sup>] = 5 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M, pH = 5 − 0.70 = 4.3, which rounds to 4.

qs.stem: Electricity is passed through an acidic solution of Cu<sup>2+</sup> till all the Cu<sup>2+</sup> was exhausted, leading to the deposition of 300 mg of Cu metal. However, a current of 600 mA was continued to pass through the same solution for another 28 minutes by keeping the total volume of the solution fixed at 200 mL. The total volume of oxygen evolved at STP during the entire process is _____ mL. (Nearest integer) [Given: Cu<sup>2+</sup>(aq) + 2e<sup>−</sup> → Cu(s), E°<sub>red</sub> = +0.34 V; O<sub>2</sub>(g) + 4H<sup>+</sup> + 4e<sup>−</sup> → 2H<sub>2</sub>O, E°<sub>red</sub> = +1.23 V; molar mass of Cu = 63.54 g mol<sup>−1</sup>; molar mass of O<sub>2</sub> = 32 g mol<sup>−1</sup>; Faraday constant = 96500 C mol<sup>−1</sup>; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L]
steps: Anode gives O<sub>2</sub> throughout (4e<sup>−</sup> per O<sub>2</sub>). During Cu deposition: electrons = 2 × 0.300/63.54 = 9.44 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol, giving O<sub>2</sub> = 2.36 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol.
Extra 28 min at 0.6 A: Q = 0.6 × 1680 = 1008 C = 1.045 × 10<sup>−2</sup> mol e<sup>−</sup>, giving O<sub>2</sub> = 2.61 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol (water now splits at both electrodes).
Total O<sub>2</sub> = 4.97 × 10<sup>−3</sup> mol; V = 4.97 × 10<sup>−3</sup> × 22400 ≈ 111 mL.

qs.stem: X and Y are the number of electrons involved, respectively during the oxidation of I<sup>−</sup> to I<sub>2</sub> and S<sup>2−</sup> to S by acidified K<sub>2</sub>Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub>. The value of X + Y is __________.
steps: Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup> accepts 6 e<sup>−</sup> (2Cr<sup>6+</sup> → 2Cr<sup>3+</sup>), so the balanced equation 6I<sup>−</sup> + Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup> + 14H<sup>+</sup> → 2Cr<sup>3+</sup> + 3I<sub>2</sub> + 7H<sub>2</sub>O transfers X = 6 electrons.
Likewise 3S<sup>2−</sup> + Cr<sub>2</sub>O<sub>7</sub><sup>2−</sup> + 14H<sup>+</sup> → 3S + 2Cr<sup>3+</sup> + 7H<sub>2</sub>O transfers Y = 6 electrons.
